question: Moldova, which has been an EU candidate country since June 2022 and was invited by the Commission in November 2023 to open accession negotiations, is working to meet the accession criteria, with a focus on administrative reform, democratisation and combating corruption.

Considering that around 60 % of Moldovans living abroad are resident in the EU, including 130 000 in Italy, legislative initiative No 65, which would limit postal voting to citizens in the USA and Canada alone, raises concerns as potentially clashing with the principles of access to universal and fair voting. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.

Is the Commission actively monitoring the Moldovan legislative process and does it know the details of legislative initiative No 65; was it involved or consulted on this by officials in Chișinău; and what is its position on limiting postal voting to certain foreign countries, to the exclusion of others – including all the EU countries?

Will it intervene with this partner country on this matter and inform the EU and international bodies on this law, if approved, concerning the implications for the voting rights of Moldovans living abroad?
answer: The Commission is actively monitoring the legislative developments in the Republic of Moldova (hereinafter ‘Moldova’), notably in light of the formal launch of accession negotiations on 25 June 2024 (1) and the commitment to align its legislation with EU standards, including those related to electoral law. The Commission reports on the progress done by Moldova every year in its Enlargement Report (2).

Additionally, the President of the Parliament of Moldova has sought the expertise of the Venice Commission by requesting an opinion on the partial implementation of the postal vote. This request was made through the framework of the Quick Response Mechanism tool of the Partnership for Good Governance (3), a program financed by the EU.

It is understood that a draft opinion would be submitted to the next plenary session of the Venice Commission for its adoption. The Commission will continue to closely follow this process and the subsequent findings of the Venice Commission. The Commission will also continue to support Moldova on its EU path and remain in close contact with Moldova on any new legislative developments.
